subject: Usage multiplier promo and threshold smoothing
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@nimblehealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nimblehealth.com
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Usage multiplier promo and threshold smoothing

Grace —

Thanks for the call earlier. Procurement asked me to get a clear written description of how the onboarding credits and your proposed ‘usage multiplier’ would convert to our invoices across the first 6 months. Smart finance folks at Nimble want examples that show: (1) how credits reduce billed spend each month, (2) how you avoid cliffing when we cross a threshold mid-quarter, and (3) whether surge credits apply when we run a one-off higher load during launch.

Can you put together a short worked example (tokens -> credits -> invoice) and confirm whether the multiplier is refundable or is a prepayment that rolls into committed spend? We also need an estimate for total committed tokens to include in our PO.

Samir
Head of Product
NimbleHealth

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage multiplier promo and threshold smoothing

Samir —

Appreciate the specificity. I put a short proposal and a worked model together (attached). Summary:

- Pilot window: 60 days.
- Onboarding surge credit: 1.5x of your month-0 average usage applied as one-time credit across the first invoice month.
- Multiplier promo: for the first 3 months after go-live we apply a multiplier to usage-derived credits (example: 1.25x credits on billed tokens) which effectively lowers net per-token cost vs list prices.
- Threshold smoothing (no cliffing): if your monthly usage crosses a tier mid-bill-cycle we prorate the tier transition across days and apply a smoothing factor to avoid abrupt jumps.
- Credits treatment: onboarding surge credits are non-refundable but are applied against invoices as token-credit offsets; multiplier promo credit is a bill-side adjustment (not an automatic prepayment) and is visible on the invoice line item.

Quick worked example from the model (see tab "Examples"): if you consume 250M tokens in Month 1 with list price $0.0008/token and a 1.25x multiplier on credits, the invoice shows list charge for 250M, then -X credits applied, net payable = Y. The attached spreadsheet has line-by-line math.

Next steps: 1) If this rough structure works I'll loop in Legal to prepare a short term-sheet and DocuSign; 2) we can lock in a PO target (ballpark we usually see customers pick a 6–12 month committed corridor).

Attachment: 2027-03-17-multiplier-model.xlsx (spreadsheet with examples)

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@nimblehealth.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage multiplier promo and threshold smoothing

Looping in a slightly revised commercial option from our side:

- Option A (Grace's baseline): 60-day pilot, 1.5x onboarding surge credit, 3-month 1.25x multiplier on credits.
- Option B (preferred for NimbleHealth's expected bursty profile): 90-day pilot, onboarding bridge credit equal to 1.25x month-0 usage applied across first two invoices, then a 6-month tapered multiplier (1.4x -> 1.2x -> 1.1x -> 1.05x -> 1.0x -> 1.0x) to smooth economics and reduce churn risk. This avoids a single cliff and rewards sustained usage.

We can also include a committed corridor (e.g., 3–6 month baseline commit) with a smaller per-token discount in exchange for a refundable credit escrow in case of underspend. If procurement needs PO language, we can add an exhibit describing invoice offsets and the smoothing formula.

Two asks for Nimble: (1) procurement timeline — when do you need the PO? (2) can Nimble share a rough expected first quarter token curve so we can draft the taper schedule?

-Karthik
Director, Commercials
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir@nimblehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nimblehealth.com, Maya Rao <maya@nimblehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 14:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage multiplier promo and threshold smoothing

Thanks both — good options. A couple of clarifications from finance:

1) Multiplier vs bridge credit — finance prefers bridge-credit style (applied as a dollar/token offset for first N tokens) because it's easier for our accounting team to reconcile against P&L; they'd rather avoid 'multiplier' language on the invoice unless it's an explicit line item. Is that possible?

2) Refundable vs non-refundable — can we make a portion of the onboarding bridge credit refundable if we miss a usage commitment by more than 30% in the first 6 months? Procurement asked for a simple clawback mechanism.

3) PO timing — procurement needs a term-sheet and exhibit by 2027-04-15 to process a PO.

We're leaning toward Option B given the bursty rollout; if you can present Option B with bridge-credit wording and a simple pro-rated clawback, we can route it to legal next week. Also send a DocuSign link when ready.

Samir

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@nimblehealth.com>, procurement@nimblehealth.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage multiplier promo and threshold smoothing

Samir / procurement team —

Thanks — attached is a concise term-sheet and a cleaned-up model that uses bridge-credit language and includes a simple clawback: if actual cumulative usage over months 1–6 is <70% of the committed baseline, we prorate the bridge credit and refund the difference to Nimble (or apply as a credit against the next billing cycle if you prefer). Key points:

- Commercial: Option B with 90-day pilot, bridge credit = 1.25x month-0 usage applied across first two invoices, tapered credit schedule for months 3–8 (model attached).
- Clawback: refundable portion explicitly called out; refundable amount only applies to the initial bridge credit (not to regular invoice discounts).
- Accounting-friendly invoices: bridge credit appears as a separate credit line with numeric token/dollar offsets so your FP&A can reconcile easily.
- Timeline: we'll publish DocuSign link by EOD — Legal has pre-approved a short exhibit for PO language.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/link/NTYzLWRvYy1zaWdu
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4832
Attachment: 2027-03-18-redwood-term-sheet.pdf

If that aligns I'll drop in a 30-minute legal/finance sync for next week to iron the exhibit language.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Looks good. I circulated the term-sheet to procurement and legal this morning; they asked for the same DocuSign link which I have. Expecting to have an internal PO routed by 2027-04-12 at the latest. We'll confirm the month-0 usage estimate by Friday so you can lock the bridge-credit numbers.
